notes.title: 7/24 - Project Update
notes.notes:
Hello! I know there has been a lack of updates for about a month or two.
The project is just not moving that much as we prepare for the demo launch.

The open signups for the playtest is closed. Everyone who has access, is still in, please continue to help! It's very much appreciated.

Moving forward, we plan to drop the demo proper on August 5th. This playtest is the same as the demo and although reflects the game, these levels will not be in the game as they are. This is pretty much a vertical slice/tech demo... not so much a "beta" if that makes sense.

I want to take a few steps back and start clean with the project and game building. Especially as the narrative continues to be written and re-written, starting clean with production is going to make a lot more sense. Especially from an optimization point of view. Steam Deck is playable but kind of crap to be honest, anything under 60 fps is unacceptable. So this is probably the biggest reason of them all.

The demo will be "Windows Only" ... so no steam deck.... but the playtest will continue to allow for it. I don't want the players to have a bad initial experience.

The main theme/opening track to our OST has been worked on and we are preparing to announce it to the world too, you can get a preview here:

[previewyoutube=v_Nu38g2MYw;leftthumb][/previewyoutube]

Again, we welcome feedback. We're very dependent on the players to tell us what works as we are about as small of a developer as can be with little resource. We read and try to respond to everything!

Thanks so much, I'm at comic-con this week trying to find more help to make this thing better....
we're still pretty far from having a game but I think the play test is a good "demo" of what it will be. And I hope it's fun!

One more thing, for those of you in San Diego, we will be showing the game at UCSD on the 29th at Atkins Hall from 5:30PM to 9PM. Come talk to me or send your friends! Thanks - Brandon

notes.title: 3/29 more adjustments, bug fixes, notes.
notes.notes:
- vivi is about 10% faster than previously
- jump physics adjustments, added 10% to jump height 15% to double jump height. gravity is applied on jump, previously was removed. originally had it.
- naming in the options menu for graphics are now set to standard names rather than numbers which was confusing when low numbers meant better gfx etc...

- It is recommended to not use FXAA as the anti-alias but it is the default. I think TSR looks best over here.(this is probably the biggest source of the blurriness)

- I think the majority of the issues are also with nvidia cards which i do not have a machine i can test with at the moment. this probably requires tuning, dlss is better for it for sure. it will probably be in for the next round of play testing.

- a lot of people are requesting a borderless windowed mode from in game options. i have to look into that a bit more... For now you should be able to load up the game at a particular windowed resolution via commandline. For Example: NecroKnight.exe -windowed -ResX=1920 -ResY=1080

notes.title: 3/22 - Post GDC Patch Notes
notes.notes:
We are back at it! (By we I mean Me, but including you!)

GDC was a great learning opportunity, and just like the last show I hope MQ becomes twice as awesome as a result. There was a lot of easy changes that I can grant right away, so this build is updated with the following tuning changes/additions. most of this is will be first trialed on the dagger than we will apply it to the other weapons.

- dagger is tuned to be slightly more snappy.
- dagger vfX added (needs work)
- no core mechanics use "stamina". only "dash" uses stamina. some weapons use stamina.
- contact hits* (currently only the dagger), the player will extend their hitbox to allow for contact hits loosening up the combat system in favor of the player
- two mystery rooms were added to the map. (proof of concept testing)

Immediate Roadmap:

New weapons are in the pipe, and I am going to redesign some of the lock and keys to be a bit more localized. (ie. players assume the red key is close to red lock).
The game begins a bit differently, there will be an optional tutorial level added as well.
Narrative lines have not been updated to reflect the story changes yet. They will be shortly.
More lines for the NPCs and Quests are coming soon.
More polish is needed, VFX and SFX/music will get some much needed attention.
Game/Level Design will undergo much more attention from a narrative lens.

THANK YOU TO EVERYONE I MET AT GDC! 

I am beyond exhausted and am continuing to recover, but the work has been cut out... and we are going to shape this game into something better, then repeat, until we have a great game. That's just how it goes. Thanks for playtesting, ETA for Demo release is May 1st.

notes.title: Update Notes for 2/22
notes.notes:
New environments have been added! Depth of Field has returned.

- There is now like a bottom level sewer like place. that is accessible through an activatable door. A large mushroom NPC is hanging out there now, it will get a lot more NPCs soon.

- There is a large room now that adjoins the dragon room to the basement, the door must be opened from the dragon side to unlock the map. There is kind of a heavy battle in this room, it's still very simple but can get a bit tense with so many NPCs. I want to demonstrate an AOE spell here, it will look really cool in a trailer.

- The chapel no longer blocks the back door, it leads out to the cemetery now.. and there are no NPCs but it is quite the interesting outdoor environment. The boss save room also exits out this way to create a more connected loop.

I guess it took a few days to get this new update together.
To be honest getting rejected by Day of the Devs left me super heart broken.
I really wanted to be a part of that show, in San Francisco, where my heart definitely is.
We will carry on. I most likely will cut short my trip back up to SF, the game probably isn't there yet if I can't get on a top 100 list.

Anyway, hope you enjoy the update. I can't let it effect my work. I shouldn't have applied to shows knowing the emotional cost effecting my productivity. There was no way to know that.

Even more NPCs, maybe new weapons, and content creep coming soon. The floodgates for new content has been opened for a few more days before I clamp down and start optimizing with another round of polish for GDC. im gonna make someone elses showcase look better than theirs... at least im gonna try.... i made the mistake of running on a rtx2060mobile at my first show... im about to turn all the options on for the next one on a rtx4090mobile.

notes.title: 2/15 patch notes, new npcs, camera changes, near future plans.
notes.notes:
so these flying type npcs are in now, i left one in at the chapel entrance. that makes that encounter maybe too difficult to start. but ill let it slide for a day.

i added a lich wizard in the west throne room. this will be replaced by a lich king with a sword i think. this npc will drop the red key. the red key will soon open the illuminated door in the same area. keys will be a bit more localized towards their usage shortly. so there will be some expansion of the current map in all directions, the feeling is way too linear, and i dont think the boss fight should be the end, i think there should be equally interesting things going in all directions, so it never feels like you took the right or wrong one...

camera changes... in more expansive areas ive pulled the camera back. basically the bigger the area the more view you will get now. this actually helps the game feel a ton. such a small thing. this will be played with a lot more.

there just needs to be more props, movement, fx, etc... all the polish ive done, and it feels like i need twice as much. i need to keep interjecting the narrative back into the players face at some sort of cadence so they know their significance in the story. maybe more lore drops. interactions. a quest log... something. its a whole missing leg to this thing imho and not an exact science. the best i can do is fill in the gaps to support it.

i feel like i got a week to tidy up all the text to send it off for a translation. then do some submissions. refocus on optimizations and compatibility, marketing/promoting.... so i think things need to pick up its pace in the next 2 weeks, lots of new construction and probably breaking things. but in the end, a stronger demo (hopefully).

notes.title: minor big changes.
notes.notes:
continuing to tune things up a bit...

mana and health bars grow in size with max ups. this is to help communicate that level ups actually give you something.

the interactions have move to on release, so we can use hold time.
effect items now have a tap to use, hold to loot functionality.

notes.title: 12/24 Last Update of the Year
notes.notes:
Thank you!

It's been an interesting year. Looking back at where the game started and how many times I thought the game would be good enough to show the world only to be humbled again and again. We are making so much progress right now and the game is really transforming right before my eyes.

The changes in this build are:

- You can now spend coin!! 
- All NPCs now hit a lot harder
- The intro to the chapel now has a new music track from Vilakshan!

Vilakshan has been gracious to allow me to use some of his music as we work towards a playable demo. This track is just a test placement, I think we want something else here, but holy smokes it is well executed guitar! Please support his music!!! http://www.youtube.com/@VilakshanKandwal

The next month will be furthering tuning of existing gameplay and upgrading the visual fidelity across the board, a lot of stuff is just in placeholder state and needs to move closer to something final. 

I personally believe the game needs to feel much more challenging than where it stands today, but I wanted people to be able to play through easily to the end. The game is quite fun when the difficulty is high.

Thanks again, hope you have a nice holiday season! Happy New Year! Development continues in 2025!

notes.title: 12/17 - More feedback changes.... mostly player focused.

--- this might be too heavy handed, let me know if it makes things less responsive/sticky
+ archer range shortened, should be harder for them to try to shoot when offscreen
+ louder impact and yelp when pc is hit

I am always reluctant to change locomotion stuff because it can be so impactful with level design and spacing. Please let me know if you run into trouble!

Coming next will be level/geometry and lighting changes! 

-B

notes.title: Update Notes for Nov 21.
notes.notes:
Hello MQ PlayTesters,

It's been awhile and a lot of work has been done. After initial playtests it became clear that leaning more into the Castlevania style of gameplay is what was really desired by players. So the game is in the process of evolving that way, changing the way things spawn and loot. How the camera moves through the level. How levels are built. I mean, it's a lot, and it's in progress so you might notice some initial wonkiness.

Our big target is the Sac Gamers Expo, where we will be showing the game off for the first time! Before that event we will be doing a small let's play presentation here with the San Diego Unreal Developers Group. I have a new level pretty much constructed and some NPCs I am dreaming up. So, in all likelihood 'the demo' level (whats playable here) will not be what we will be showing publicly. But it is a good place to see if the changes have made a difference to making the gameplay better.

So please test! The menu is full of all the weapons and spells that is all unlocked. I highly recommend playing around with dash and levitate together. And have fun, let me know what you like hate and wish would be better. I love fun ideas, so please share!

-Brandon

notes.title: Update Notes for Oct. 21, 2024
notes.notes:
UI for a SPELLBOOK has been added!

It can be found in the pause menu temporarily. There are four spells in there and they're repeated to test the scrolling list view. I think this will eventually extend to the other slots so you could actually collect weapons/shields/bows and swap them too. I already really like having all the spells available to me.

Controller Compatibility Testing Report.

Use Steam input for all non XBox/Windows controllers. It works perfectly for Dualsense, Switch Pro, and Steam Deck. The game plays great on Steam Deck!!!

Levitation !

All weapons usable in the air can also be used during levitate and it should break the levitation too. I am really enjoying using Levitation as like a brake and recharge, with dash being more like gas and double jump like another brake. I would love to start developing more platforming to pair with this. I'm open to ideas!

Until next update! Thanks for playtesting!
-Brandon

notes.notes:
Welcome New Playtesters!

Please fill out the feedback form at the end of the demo!!! Or feel free to email as well!

The magic system has gotten some attention and there are now 3 total spells in the demo. The initial starter spell is meant to compliment the bow and arrow in balance. It does less damage but costs a self renewing resource "mana" the cool down is a bit slower but its still an instant attack spell.

The next two spells are not instant. They have spell times which means they can be interrupted (or canceled via b button or moving). These initial spells are powerful in their own ways and I am excited for you to find them try them out, let me know how they feel, too! There will be many many more spells, self buffs, debuff attacks, aoe, etc... etc... but for now, we only have 3,

The goal is still to push out a demo soon, so more iteration on things like weapons and combat, more polish, more qol, and some plot lines are being constructed!! Stay tuned! Thanks for playing!

notes.notes:
Major Changes!

- Bow/Arrow now occupies the "RT" slot.
- Shield is given immediately at level start.

- A 3 Stat system is in place (but not hooked up completely). Brute/Magic/Range are values you can choose to allocate to during gameplay. Similar to Dead Cell's scroll system, but maybe even simpler to start.

- There are some new bugs introduced, so there will be a few quick fix patches coming in.

Roadmap:

- Spells are identified as something that there needs more variety to 'demo'
- Some more (optional) level content will be added
- Coins should be able to buy stuff

---- amongst a huge back log of so many things... 

I personally feel like these additional mechanisms although simple really help the experience feel more complete. Character development is a huge in what the story/narrative will need to assist in.  Still needs a lot of UI work.

The November target would be a submission to some Indie Festivals coming on later next year which would need to happen now. As usual, lagging on the website, marketing, pitch, etc... etc... I will really need that in place by November when I want the Demo live while I submit...

I think 10/15 is the date I would like to set the playtest to open to the public, so we can have more feedback to work towards a more polished demo.

notes.title: Update Notes for 10/8/2024
notes.notes:
Some pretty big changes today.

-- Shields are being implemented as a parry/block mechanic.

There will be a parry window where shields will cancel damage.
Block will be after the parry window and will mitigate damage on a scale.
It is based on length of button press. Currently, < 0.5 seconds is considered a parry.

-- Boss Room gets chandeliers!

There is now a place to stand and maybe even get some STA back. The wizard also takes his actions
within knife distance of the lamps. He generally stays a bit closer to the ground or on one of those two planes to make hitting him hopefully a bit easier.

A lot has changed, especially with the shields and xp leveling effecting stats... things do feel slightly more robust but i am sure bugs have been introduced as well. If you spot any please let me know!

Otherwise, I hope these changes are in the right direction and make the game a little better! 

Until next time!

notes.title: Update 10/6/24 - B
notes.notes:
I am testing the ogre's being somewhat "evasive".

There is now a chance for them to jump back or roll forward before attacking, along with just attacking. This is to guess if you jump back or slide forward as well. It is a bit of rock paper scissors, but the player still has plenty of window to have the upper hand.

I am receiving a lot of feedback about the enemies being too easy, too predictable. It is a rule that making a "smarter ai" is not usually more fun. It needs to be entertaining is the top goal. On the other hand I am receiving feedback that enemies are a bit too hard and difficult to react to as well.

So this is a bit of a test to see if its more well received. It is still certainly easy to avoid for me... But every once in awhile it gets me :) and maybe that's enough... it is also the game's introduction, and i think the expectation of easy to smash needs to be met as well.

Some of these ideas will carry forward with other human-like enemies too and it will be interesting to see if its something that can be dialed up a bit.

Anyway, hope you enjoy it. It's probably again too subtle to make an impact. I'll play around with more ideas over here, feel free to chime in your feedback, ideas, criticisms, etc...

-Brandon

notes.title: Playtest Update 10/5/2024
notes.notes:
Hail, MegaQuest Fans !!!

Todays build offers some major adjustments with a subtle effect currently. 
XP Level-ing is now in the game !!!

The only weapon that is level modified currently is the rusty dagger. I will do a pass through and tune the weapons soon and have them all doing that in short order.

When you level, you now will get more max hitpoints, mana, and stamina. 
I will adjust regen values in the short future.

Players were not arriving at the boss with enough hitpoints and my heart containers were a little too well hidden. There is now a lot more incentive to kill everything and even grind out levels if you like that play style.  The system offers a lot more than it takes away and it was an easy decision to turn it on.

I don't think it really has that big of an effect other than it makes the endgame a little easier.
the bosses are still a little bit cheese so i will try to tune them further, again in short order...

Now, on a very casual play through you end up at the boss room with about 200 HP as opposed to 100 if you didn't find any heart containers. I left in all the heart containers, but I might change some to mana boosts or other goodies to be discovered.

We are aiming to be ready for a public playtest on 10/15 in anticipation of releasing the demo.

Thanks for play testing!!!
- Brandon
